# `resolve` captures state: a change in its output reruns the target, and a
# failing resolve plans a create. `values` turns a JSON object into outputs.
bit remote
stdout '^remote ▶ '
grep '\Av1\n\z' applied.txt

bit remote
stdout '^remote · no changes$'

cp state.txt.v2 state.txt
bit --plan remote
stdout '^remote ~ .*\(resolve: resource state drifted\)$'
bit remote
stdout '^remote ▶ .*\(resolve: resource state drifted\)$'
grep '\Av2\n\z' applied.txt

rm state.txt
bit --plan remote
stdout '^remote \+ '

bit show
stdout '^ *show │ version=1\.2 name=demo$'

-- BUILD.bit --
remote = exec {
  command = "cp state.txt applied.txt"
  resolve = "cat state.txt"
}

info = exec {
  command = "true"
  values = "cat info.json"
}

show = exec {
  command = "echo version=#{info.version} name=#{info.name}"
}
-- state.txt --
v1
-- state.txt.v2 --
v2
-- info.json --
{"version": "1.2", "name": "demo"}
